Discussions included organising a Mexican business mission to India in early 2027 to improve commercial ties. India had a trade surplus with Mexico, largely due to exports in autos and pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Centre open to changes in DPDP law to  protect press freedom, says Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.desc: The Centre aims to amend the Digital Personal Data Protection law to address concerns raised by news publishers. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that the law does not limit press freedom. This response follows a Supreme Court notice regarding a petition from the Digital News Publishers Association and others. Publishers argue the lack of exemption for journalism could jeopardize investigative reporting and confidential sources.

articles.title: India's industrial growth slows to 6.7% in September from 8% in August
articles.desc: India's Index of Industrial Production for September recorded a growth rate of 6.7%. This figure represents a decline from August's 8%. Key contributors to this growth include the manufacture of motor vehicles and electrical equipment, among others. The manufacture of rubber and plastics also played a significant role in September's performance. These statistics were released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

articles.title: What do you want from the Budget?
articles.desc: The BBC spoke to people in Cardiff and County Durham about their concerns ahead of the chancellor's Autumn Budget.

articles.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
articles.desc: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation.

articles.title: Former Conservative chancellor unsure Budget will 'fix big problems'
articles.desc: Sir Jeremy Hunt spoke to BBC Breakfast about his hopes and qualms ahead of John Healey's autumn Budget.

articles.title: Cabinet hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% with Rs 10,000 crore allocation; check key announcements
articles.desc: DA hike: The Union Cabinet has approved several development schemes totaling Rs 29,267 crores for various initiatives. Among these is a Rs 10,016 crore increase in Dearness Allowance for Central government employees. The DA will benefit about 48 lakh employees and 68 lakh pensioners, with hikes effective from July 1, 2026.

articles.title: Delivery Hero raises full-year forecast again on strong Q3 growth
articles.desc: The company now expects gross merchandise value (GMV), a common metric for delivery firms measuring the total value of all goods sold through the market place, to grow 10%-12% this year, up from a previous forecast of 9%-11%.

articles.title: Agentic AI can cut banks' transaction monitoring workload by up to 50%: McKinsey
articles.desc: Banks could reduce the human effort required for transaction monitoring investigations by 30-50% by deploying agentic artificial intelligence (AI), while improving the quality and consistency of compliance reports, according to a report by McKinsey.

articles.title: AI chips worth $12.1 million seized at Malaysia airport, customs authority says

articles.title: India's soybean imports surge to record as domestic prices rally
articles.desc: India's soybean imports significantly increased to 1.1 million metric tons in 2025/26 compared to the previous year. Rising domestic prices prompted Indian mills to enhance their overseas purchases of soybeans. The majority of these imports originated from Niger, which became the largest exporter to India.

articles.title: China's CXMT to start advanced AI memory production despite poor yields
articles.desc: The decision highlights China's intense shortage of the AI memory chips, which are essential to a government-backed push to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's AI processors at scale amid US curbs on access to foreign-made technology.

articles.title: TPG pursues $5 billion acquisition of British data centre group Ark: FT
articles.desc: Global alternative asset manager TPG is in talks to buy British data centre group Ark from Elliott Investment Management at a valuation of about $5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: GST clarification on foreign investor brokerage offers sentiment boost, analysts say
articles.desc: The Indian government has clarified that brokerage paid by overseas clients may qualify as an export service. This could help foreign investors avoid the 18% goods and services tax on brokerage fees. Analysts suggest this clarification is sentimentally positive amid significant foreign outflows from Indian stocks. There is ongoing speculation regarding potential cuts in capital gains tax ahead of the federal budget.

articles.title: Indian IT firms poised to benefit from enterprise AI adoption as infrastructure costs rise: Report
articles.desc: Indian information technology (IT) companies are well-positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) by enterprises, as rising infrastructure investments and funding requirements increase financial risks for companies building and operating AI computing capacity, according to a research report by Anand Rathi.

articles.title: India, Mexico sign terms of reference to kickstart trade pact negotiations
articles.desc: India and Mexico have signed the Terms of Reference to initiate negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement. This agreement aims to enhance bilateral trade and investment opportunities between the two countries. Key negotiating areas include market access, customs procedures, and trade facilitation measures. Both delegations discussed organizing a Mexican business mission to India in early 2027.
